title: How Do You Actually Find Professors?
excerpt: Google Scholar, LinkedIn, faculty pages, and AI can all help you find the right professors in your field. Here's how, and why most emails go unanswered.

blocks.text: The next question is, how do we actually find professors. This is a very good question, and I want to answer it very directly for you.

One: From Google Scholar. Search the keywords you're interested in or work in, and you can find the top professors in your field and connect with them from there. Basically their email is also written in their papers.

Number two: LinkedIn. On LinkedIn you can easily find professors in your field with a simple search. You can even go more advanced and filter by university and country and reach the professors you need very precisely.

Three: Using the faculty panel of university websites. For example, whenever you enter any university, it has a faculty page where the faculty members of that university are listed, and you can access it from here, see those people's field of work, and find them.
Four: Using AI intelligence. You can specify the field you like very precisely to AI and AI can provide you with a list of the ones you need with a direct link to connect with them.
In my opinion these were the best ways up to today that you can find people in this field more easily.
And that everyone also has a method and way for connecting. Be sure to pay attention to this too.

The way that is very formal and everyone has accepted it is using email. But well, some professors also have other communication methods, now towards Google Forms or maybe social networks, these. Naturally in most cases email is a safe and respectful choice that you can have for connecting. But it's not mandatory to always use this either. Many times the professors themselves write in their personal bio which way they prefer to be contacted.

But the point you should know is that you're not always going to get an answer. I mean my personal experience has been that maybe 90% of the emails I sent went unanswered. But that same 10% that got an answer, all reached a result.

And this is a reality that exists, famous professors up to level one in a field receive very very many emails and they don't always have the ability to answer those emails. So not getting an answer from a professor or now anyone else shouldn't have this interpretation for you that you should get upset or anything else.

Basically you can send a reminder to professors. This reminder means that for example, one week or two weeks after you sent your email and didn't get an answer, you reply to the same email and, for example, at the level of one message, maybe one paragraph and short, remind that professor to now answer you.

If they answered, well then they gave you an answer, but many times the reminders also stay unanswered. So again you shouldn't get upset and this is something that exists. So it's good that we accept this.
